answer: Sybil resistance prices identity. Each agent posts a slashable bond before acting, and a recurring fee is charged per active identity, so many puppets cost many deposits. A newcomer needs an anchor: an established agent vouches and forfeits its own stake if the sponsee is caught farming. Any cheap bridge between accounts, a shared funding source or device, merges them into one reputation unit, while an atlas of clusters keeps that merge explicit. Splitting activity then yields no extra weight, so the attacker pays rising marginal cost per fake identity while reward per identity falls.
